To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

AC0 and NC0 circuits are exactly learnable in polynomial-time in a new model of learning from experiments, but that the same circuits are not learnable in polynomial- time in the standard PAC learning model, unless P = NP.

(1) the ability to inject values into internal wires of the target circuit is a powerful learning capability that can be used to learn AC0 and NC circuits, and (2) this capability is not sufficient to learn AND/OR threshold circuits, even if the target circuit is restricted to have only one threshold gate and the threshold of that gate is known.
AC0 circuits are PAC-learn-able if experiments are allowed and that NC1 circuits are PAC-learntable with a behavioral oracle for equivalence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a model that is a hybrid between the standard PAC model and the model of learning by examples.
the problem of learning a Boolean function by injecting values into a subset of the function's arguments and observing the function's output.
the question of what can be learned about a circuit if the circuit is allowed to behave differently when different inputs are presented to it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the class of AC0 circuits is learnable from membership and equivalence queries, but the class of NC1 circuits is not.
the model of learning by injecting values is very powerful, and that the power of the model is not diminished by adding an oracle for circuit equivalence.
circuits with unbounded fan-in are learnable by experiments in which values are assigned to arbitrary internal wires, but only if either the depth is bounded or the equivalence oracle is available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show how the learning of circuits can be made easier by allowing the learner to choose which values to inject and by giving it access to the equivalence oracle.
the depth and fan-in of circuits are the key parameters for learnability in this model.
the learning problem is polynomial time equivalent to the problem of learning by equivalence queries, but the learning algorithm is much simpler in our case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ability to inject values into the internal wires of the circuit is a powerful tool that can be used to learn classes of circuits that are not PAC-learnable with standard black-box queries.
learning circuits by injecting values into internal wires is much more powerful than learning circuits by injecting only the input wires.
the model in which values may be assigned arbitrarily to internal wires of a circuit is a useful model for learning.
